anonymous_bind_disabled.title: Anonymous Bind Disabled
anonymous_bind_disabled.description: Attests that the directory server rejects anonymous bind requests (no DN, no credentials). Secure when true (OpenLDAP 'disallow bind_anon' / olcDisallows: bind_anon; ldapwhoami -x returns inappropriateAuthentication). When false the server accepts anonymous binds, letting an unauthenticated client connect and enumerate the DIT for reconnaissance.

directory_access_requires_authentication.title: Directory Operations Require Authentication
directory_access_requires_authentication.description: Attests that all directory operations require an authenticated identity ('require authc' / olcRequires: authc). Secure when true. Disabling anonymous BIND does not stop anonymous directory READS — when this is false the server still answers anonymous searches, exposing the whole tree to an unauthenticated client. This is the bypass path for anonymous_bind_disabled.

unauthenticated_empty_password_bind_reje.title: Empty-Password (Unauthenticated) Bind Rejected
unauthenticated_empty_password_bind_reje.description: Attests that a simple bind with a non-empty DN and a ZERO-length password (RFC 4513 §5.1.2 unauthenticated authentication mechanism) is rejected with unwillingToPerform/invalidCredentials. Secure when true (OpenLDAP olcAllows lacks bind_anon_cred). When false a lax server silently authenticates the client as the named DN with an empty password — an authentication bypass.

encryption_in_transit_enabled.title: Directory Channel Encrypted In Transit
encryption_in_transit_enabled.description: Whether the LDAP/directory access flow is encrypted in transit (ldaps://636 or a successfully negotiated StartTLS on 389). When false, simple bind sends the bind DN and password in cleartext over ldap://389, exposing the credential to network sniffing. Shared workspace transit-encryption attestation reused across flows.

ldap_tls_required.title: Minimum Confidentiality (TLS) Enforced on Bind
ldap_tls_required.description: Whether the directory server enforces a minimum confidentiality strength on the flow so that plaintext binds are refused (OpenLDAP olcSecurity ssf/minssf >= 128, or equivalent — e.g. AD LDAP signing/channel-binding requirement). When false, the server accepts cleartext ldap://389 binds even if TLS is available, so confidentiality depends on optional client behaviour. Interpreted from olcSecurity (ssf=0 / unset = insecure).

starttls_downgrade_prevented.title: StartTLS Downgrade Prevented
starttls_downgrade_prevented.description: Whether StartTLS on the flow cannot be stripped or downgraded by an active network attacker — i.e. TLS is mandatory (ldaps://636 enforced or StartTLS required and bind refused without it) rather than opportunistic. When false, a MITM can suppress the StartTLS upgrade and force the bind to proceed in cleartext. Interpreted attestation of the flow's resistance to transport downgrade.

tls_min_version.title: Minimum TLS Version on Directory Channel
tls_min_version.description: Minimum TLS protocol version the directory channel negotiates (olcTLSProtocolMin / nmap ssl-enum on ldaps://636 or StartTLS). The encrypted bind channel is breakable when the floor is a legacy version; SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 fire the exposure while the recommended TLS1.2/TLS1.3 do not. Canonical workspace TLS-version enum shared across flows and the gateway.

weak_tls_ciphers_disabled.title: Weak TLS Cipher Suites Disabled
weak_tls_ciphers_disabled.description: Interpreted attestation that the directory channel's cipher list excludes weak/legacy suites (NULL/aNULL/eNULL, RC4, DES/3DES, EXPORT, MD5). The assessor reads olcTLSCipherSuite (e.g. a HIGH:!aNULL:!eNULL:!MD5:!RC4 form is secure) or nmap ssl-enum output; true when only strong ciphers are offered, false when any weak/export cipher remains negotiable. Modeled as an interpreted boolean rather than a raw cipher-string match because the secure form mentions the weak tokens (as !-exclusions) and would false-fire a substring rule. Fires on false (weak ciphers still allowed).

ldap_search_filter_input_escaped.title: Search-Filter Input Escaped (RFC 4515)
ldap_search_filter_input_escaped.description: Attestation: all user-supplied input concatenated into LDAP search filters on this flow is escaped per RFC 4515 (the four metacharacters * ( ) \ and NUL) or bound via a filter encoder. When false, raw user input reaches the filter string unescaped, enabling injection of filter metachars (uid=*, )(uid=*) for authentication bypass or full-tree disclosure. Interpreted boolean (the raw filter directive is not pattern-matched), so the trigger is polarity-safe; secure value is true.

parameterized_filter_templates_used.title: Parameterized Filter Templates Used
parameterized_filter_templates_used.description: Attestation: search filters on this flow are built from parameterized templates (e.g. '(&(uid={0})(objectClass=person))' with input bound separately as data) or a dedicated filter/DN encoder API (LdapFilterEncode / LdapDistinguishedNameEncode), rather than by string concatenation of raw user input. When false, filters are assembled by concatenation — the root cause of LDAP injection. Secure value is true.

dn_input_escaped.title: DN Input Escaped (RFC 4514)
dn_input_escaped.description: Attestation: user-supplied input placed into Distinguished Names on this flow is escaped per the broader RFC 4514 metacharacter set (or allow-listed). When false, an attacker can inject DN metachars to alter the target DN of a bind or modify operation. Distinct from filter escaping because RFC 4514 covers a wider character set than RFC 4515. Secure value is true.

directory_acl_least_privilege.title: Directory ACLs Least-Privilege
directory_acl_least_privilege.description: Attested true when the directory's olcAccess/access ACLs scope read to only the principals that require it and every rule chain terminates in 'by * none' — no catch-all 'access to * by * read'. False (the firing/insecure state) means an over-permissive or catch-all read ACL exposes the whole DIT to anonymous/low-privilege clients for reconnaissance.

userpassword_attribute_read_restricted.title: userPassword Attribute Read-Restricted
userpassword_attribute_read_restricted.description: Attested true when a dedicated ACL gates the userPassword attribute (and other secrets) to 'by self =xw by anonymous auth by * none', preceding the generic read rule. False (the firing/insecure state) means userPassword falls through to a generic read clause and password hashes are readable by anonymous or low-privilege clients for offline cracking.

whole_tree_anonymous_read_disabled.title: Whole-Tree Anonymous Read Disabled
whole_tree_anonymous_read_disabled.description: Attested true when anonymous clients cannot read the full directory tree — i.e. anonymous read of the DIT is denied (no anonymous 'by * read' on '*'). False (the firing/insecure state) means an anonymous client can enumerate the entire tree, the precondition that turns an over-broad ACL into full-DIT disclosure.

bind_dn_credentials_stored_plaintext_in_.title: Bind-DN Credential Stored Plaintext in Config
bind_dn_credentials_stored_plaintext_in_.description: Attestation: the service bind-DN password is stored in plaintext in application config or environment files (e.g. a literal bindpw/ldap.password value rather than a runtime reference). Fires when true: a plaintext bind credential in config is a high-value secret whose leak grants the app's directory privileges (T1552.001 Credentials In Files). Secure (false) state: the credential is never written as cleartext in config/env. Verified by config/code audit (e.g. grep for bind.?(dn|pw|password)|ldap.*pass over the config dir).

bind_dn_credentials_externalized.title: Bind-DN Credential Externalized to Secret Manager
bind_dn_credentials_externalized.description: Attestation: the LDAP bind-DN credential is resolved at runtime from a secret manager (or a SASL EXTERNAL / GSSAPI / certificate bind is used) rather than held as a static value in the application's own configuration. Fires when false: a non-externalized, in-config bind credential is the leakable secret behind this dataFlow's directory access. Secure (true) state: credential held in a secret store, injected at runtime, and rotatable. Application-side attestation of the flow, not a slapd config key.

bind_account_least_privilege_readonly.title: Service Bind Account Least-Privilege (Read-Only)
bind_account_least_privilege_readonly.description: Attestation: the directory account used for the service bind has a least-privilege, read-only ACL scoped to only the entries/attributes the application needs, rather than a broad or directory-admin-equivalent grant. Fires when false: an over-privileged bind account widens the blast radius of a leaked credential to the whole DIT (often write). Secure (true) state: the bind DN's olcAccess grants only the minimal read it requires and terminates in 'by * none'.

userpassword_hash_scheme.title: userPassword Storage Hash Scheme
userpassword_hash_scheme.description: Storage scheme used for the userPassword attribute on this directory flow, as set by slapd olcPasswordHash (or the equivalent on FreeIPA/AD). Salted strong schemes (argon2, bcrypt, ssha/{SSHA}) resist offline cracking if the hash leaks; unsalted {SHA}, weak/unsalted {CRYPT}, and {CLEARTEXT} mean any disclosure of the attribute yields trivially-recovered passwords. The exposure fires when the scheme is one of the weak values (sha, crypt, cleartext).

account_lockout_policy_enabled.title: Account-Lockout Policy Enabled
account_lockout_policy_enabled.description: Attests that the directory bind endpoint enforces an account-lockout policy (OpenLDAP ppolicy overlay loaded with pwdLockout: TRUE and a bounded pwdMaxFailure/pwdLockoutDuration; equivalent lockout on AD/FreeIPA). Secure value is true. When false, the bind endpoint accepts unlimited authentication attempts, exposing every account to credential brute-force and password-spray over the network.

search_size_and_time_limits_bounded.title: Search Size and Time Limits Bounded
search_size_and_time_limits_bounded.description: Attests that directory search operations are bounded by enforced size and time limits (OpenLDAP olcSizeLimit/olcTimeLimit set, paged-result size.prtotal bounded, and tighter per-initiator olcLimits for anonymous/unprivileged clients). Secure value is true. When false, a single client can run unbounded searches to exhaust server resources or mass-exfiltrate the entire DIT in one query.
